headline: Leafs’ Morgan Rielly leaves game with lower-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Toronto defenseman Morgan Rielly left Saturday's game against the Montreal Canadiens with a lower-body injury after just 5:45 of ice time. Karine Hains of The Hockey News posted that he was out for the rest of the game.

Rielly's season has been quieter than the usual picture of him. He has 12 assists and no goals in 17 games so far this season, and his expected goals (the quality of the shots he's taken) is 1.44, so the missing goals are partly bad finishing. The bigger point is what he does for the Leafs. They take 47.78% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice, but their team share rises 3.82 percentage points when he plays. Toronto is already at 46.8% overall, and its results (10.1 goals above expected) look generous, so losing a player who lifts the team's play is a real concern. We don't know how long he'll be out. Going by how the coach has used his players, Jake McCabe (21:37 a night) is next in line for Rielly's minutes.
